title: Retrospective Multicenter Real-World Evaluation of Cefiderocol in the Treatment of Invasive Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Infections
summary: The bacterium Stenotrophomonas maltophilia can cause dangerous infections such as pneumonia or blood poisoning, mainly in seriously ill people and people with weakened immune defences. Many antibiotics do not work against this bacterium, and there is no generally recommended standard treatment. Cefiderocol is a newer antibiotic that works well against the bacterium in the laboratory and in animal studies, but how well it helps patients in everyday hospital care has hardly been studied. In this study, about 15 to 25 hospitals in Germany, Austria and Switzerland review the medical records of adults who were treated with cefiderocol for at least two days between June 2020 and December 2025. We mainly look at how often the infection was treated successfully. We also record how long patients stayed in hospital, whether they survived, whether the infection came back and which side effects occurred. All data are fully anonymised. Patients do not undergo any additional tests or treatments.

interventions.name: Adults (≥ 18 years) with invasive S. maltophilia infection at any anatomical site who received SM-directed therapy with a cefiderocol-containing regimen (monotherapy or combination) for at least 48 hours as part of routine care. Inclusion criteria:
